newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault V.I. sees breakeven in H2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Renault V.I. sees breakeven in H2 1997.

text.p: Renault Vehicules Industriels, the heavy-goods vehicle subsidiary of Renault SA, said on Wednesday it expected to return to break-even in the second half of 1997, but to show a loss for 1997 as a whole.

"We expect to return to balance in the second half of 1997 but overall the year will be in deficit, although there will be a very clear improvement over 1996," chairman Shemaya Levy told a news conference on Renault V.I.'s results.
Renault V.I. posted a net loss of 791 million francs for 1996 after a 712 million franc profit in 1995.
Renault V.I.'s losses will come from the European business, Levy said, as Mack Trucks is expected to at least break even after making an operating profit of 147 million francs last year.
Renault V.I. said inventories at the start of the year were in line with expectations, in contrast to the situation in the second half of 1996, when it had excess inventory of around 2,000 vehicles.
Levy said the group aimed to improve productivity by five percent to recover cost increases last year that were not passed on to clients. He said price increases were not planned.
Renault's purchases total 12 billion francs a year, and Levy said he was aiming for savings of five percent a year.
He said he also expected productivity gains from an industrial rationalisation of bus and coach operations in Annonay for which a 100 million franc charge was taken in 1996.
He said he expected orders in France to rise this year to around 40,000 from 36,000 last year, boosted by the launch of new models such as the Premium, Iliade, Agora and Magnum.
Launch costs had a negative 350 million franc impact on the operating result in 1996.
The group aims to raise exports from 7,600 vehicles last year. "The objective of 10,000 vehicles a year is within reach," he said. The group is targetting eastern and central Europe.
